content: 1. Ella (ulipristal) is administered as a single 30 mg oral tablet as soon as possible, within 120 hours (5 days) after unprotected intercourse or suspected contraceptive failure. If vomiting occurs within 3 hours of administration, consider repeating the dose. The efficacy is higher if taken within the first 72 hours post-coitus. It is not indicated for premenarche individuals, and its safety and efficacy have not been established in those under 18 years of age. 2. Ketoconazole increases the level or effect of ulipristal by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Levoketoconazole also increases the level or effect of ulipristal via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of ulipristal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Bosentan decreases the level or effect of ulipristal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism.
